Usage: shotdetect -i <video> [options]
       shotdetect qc -i <file> [options]   delivery checks (loudness ...): shotdetect qc --help

  -i, --input <file|url|->           Video file, a URL (http, rtsp, ...), or - for standard input

  -d, --detector <name>              adaptive, content, threshold, hist or hash (default: adaptive). Repeat
                                     to combine detectors, as scenedetect does: -t, -m and --filter-mode
                                     after a -d apply to that detector (-d content -t 30 -d threshold -t 8)
  --filter-mode <merge|suppress>     content: how min-scene-len is enforced (default merge)
  --drop-short-scenes                Detect without min-scene-len, then drop shots shorter than it
  --merge-last-scene                 Merge the last shot into the previous one if shorter than min-scene-len
  --downscale <n>                    Downscale frames by n (scenedetect -d); default automatic, 1 = none
  -t, --threshold <n>                content: content_val threshold (default 27)
                                     adaptive: adaptive ratio threshold (default 3)
                                     threshold: mean pixel level of a fade (default 12)
                                     hist: drop in histogram correlation (default 0.20; 0.05 with --compat 0.7.1)
                                     hash: fraction of hash bits that differ (default 0.35; 0.395 with --compat 0.7.1)
  -m, --min-scene-len <time>         Minimum shot length: frames (15), seconds (0.6s, 0.6) or HH:MM:SS.mmm (default 0.6s)
  -c, --min-content-val <n>          adaptive: minimum content_val for a cut (default 15)
      --frame-window <n>             adaptive: frames on each side to average (default 2)
  -w, --weights <h> <s> <l> <e>      content/adaptive: weights of hue, saturation, luma and edge
                                     differences in content_val (default 1 1 1 0)
  -k, --kernel-size <n>              content/adaptive: odd size >= 3 to widen edges by

result.stdout:
Usage: shotdetect qc -i <file> [options]

A file's delivery checks in one report: a text table on standard output, exit code 0 when every check passes,
3 when any is out of range (1: an error, 2: usage). Not in scenedetect.

  -i, --input <file|url>             The file to check
      --checks <list>                Comma-separated checks to run (default all): loudness, range, bars-tone, black,
                                     freeze
      --preset <name>                Loudness limits: ebu-r128 (default; -23 LUFS +/- 0.5 LU, true peak -1 dBTP),
                                     atsc-a85 (-24 LKFS +/- 2, -2 dBTP), streaming-14 or streaming-16 (+/- 1, -1 dBTP)
      --loudness-target <LUFS>       Integrated loudness target (default: the preset's)
      --loudness-tolerance <LU>      How far from the target still passes (default: the preset's)
      --true-peak-max <dBTP>         Highest true peak that passes (default: the preset's)
      --brng-max <percent>           Most pixels of any frame outside broadcast range (signalstats' BRNG:
                                     luma outside 16-235, chroma outside 16-240 at 8 bits) that passes
                                     (default 1)
      --black-min <seconds>          Shortest black span (ffmpeg's blackdetect d; default 2)
      --freeze-min <seconds>         Shortest frozen picture (ffmpeg's freezedetect d; default 2)
      --edge <seconds>               Black and frozen pictures at the head and tail, within this of the start
                                     or end, are listed, not judged (default 10)
      --require-bars-tone            Fail unless colour bars and 1 kHz line-up tone overlap in the first
                                     minute (default: bars and tone are reported, never judged)
      --json <file>                  Also write the report as JSON (- for standard output, then no table)
      --html <file>                  Also write the report as one HTML page: the checks and a timeline
      --ffmpeg-dir <folder>          FFmpeg 8's
[truncated]
